messages:
jess_sec: Erin DM'd sec — she clicked an email that looked like an OAuth approval flow asking to "approve 'Redwood CI — GitHub App'". She clicked through to choose an account and hit Allow. Can we triage?

erin_marketing: yup that was me. i clicked by mistake. it opened accounts.google.com then a redirect. i didn't type any passwords.

phish-sandbox-bot: Sandbox scan complete for https://tiny[.]link/abc123 -> Detected credential-harvest OAuth mimic. Redirects to accounts.google.com with forged params, then attempts token exchange to phishing domain phishing-redirect[.]xyz. No binary payload. IOC: phishing-redirect[.]xyz, IP 91.203.45.12.

jess_sec: Ok — immediate actions: revoke OAuth grants for Erin, sign out active sessions, revoke any GH tokens tied to that grant. Raj, can you check CloudTrail/Okta/GSuite audit for token exchange and suspicious API activity? Oliver, can you assess repo/service access and rotate deploy keys if needed.

raj_sre: On it. Running queries now: checking Okta OAuth grants, GSuite admin audit, CloudTrail. Looking for token exchange events and unusual IPs.

oliver_eng: Copy. I'll enumerate Erin's org permissions and recent pushes. If there was a token with repo scope, we'll remove it and rotate keys.

okta-bot: Action performed: terminated sessions for erin@redwood.com (actioned by jess_sec).

jess_sec: Erin — please confirm you can still access your Google account normally and remove the app from https://myaccount.google.com/permissions. If you can't, we'll escalate SsPR. Also set a new password and ensure 2FA is enabled.

erin_marketing: I can login. I removed the app and signed out of other sessions. thanks.

raj_sre: Quick findings: Okta shows an OAuth grant at 2026-06-18T11:42:03Z originating from IP 91.203.45.12 (known proxy cluster). GH API shows an installation token issued to external app id 9876 with scopes repo,user and last_used 2026-06-18T11:42:10Z. No CreateAccessKey or AssumeRole events tied to erin@ in CloudTrail in the last 24h.

jess_sec: Good. Block 91.203.45.12 in perimeter and email gateway, add phishing-redirect[.]xyz to denylist. Create a detection rule to alert on OAuth grants from anonymous/proxy IP ranges and for external redirector domains.

phish-sandbox-bot: Additional IOC: observed redirect chain includes phishing-redirect[.]xyz -> accounts.google.com?client_id=.. -> token POST to exfiltrator[.]host. Classified as credential-harvest. No executable payload.

oliver_eng: I removed Erin from org membership temporarily and revoked the app via GH admin. Rotated deploy keys for infra-repo and rotated service principal tokens that Erin had access to. Will re-add Erin after device attestation.

jess_sec: Logged actions and tracking under INC-2026-045 and TKT-8123. Post-incident list: 1) org-wide reminder about OAuth consent flows, 2) email gateway rule for 'Approve access' phishing pattern, 3) phishing microtraining assigned to marketing, 4) implement OAuth-grant anomaly detection, 5) rotate any tokens where Erin had admin rights (done/ongoing).

erin_marketing: really sorry everyone, thanks for the quick response.

jess_sec: No worries — no blame. We'll send a company-wide FYI and short checklist to follow if you accidentally approve an app.

raj_sre: I'll export full audit logs for the security packet and attach to INC-2026-045. ETA ~2h.

jess_sec: Great — thanks team :thumbsup: If there are no other asks I'll close this thread and update the incident with remediation notes and timeline.

oliver_eng: I'll follow up with a list of rotated keys and repos.

phish-sandbox-bot: Closing sandbox analysis entry for tiny[.]link/abc123. Classification: credential-harvest (low persistence).

jess_sec: closing for now.
